title: Meta-analysis of fecal metagenomes reveals global microbial signatures that are specific for colorectal cancer
what_they_do: 8-study CRC metagenome meta-analysis; LOSO and cross-study transfer of LASSO classifiers; thresholds set at fixed FPR on training data; reports AUROC and disease specificity
how_we_differ: Reports cross-study AUROC; threshold fixed on training data, does not quantify realised specificity drift per site or propose site-level threshold adaptation

title: Metagenomic analysis of colorectal cancer datasets identifies cross-cohort microbial diagnostic signatures and a link with choline degradation
what_they_do: Cross-cohort CRC classifiers (RF) across 7 cohorts; LODO; control augmentation to improve specificity
how_we_differ: AUROC-centred; no label-free per-site operating-point recalibration

title: Machine learning meta-analysis of large metagenomic datasets: tools and biological insights
what_they_do: MetAML: cross-study and LODO prediction of disease from metagenomes across 8 diseases
how_we_differ: AUROC/accuracy only; no thresholds

title: Potential of fecal microbiota for early-stage detection of colorectal cancer
what_they_do: Metagenomic CRC classifier with external validation; combination with FOBT at fixed specificity
how_we_differ: Single fixed cut-off; external specificity reported but not adapted

title: Meta-analysis of gut microbiome studies identifies disease-specific and shared responses
what_they_do: 28 16S case-control studies; per-study classifiers; shared vs disease-specific signals
how_we_differ: Within-study AUROC; no transfer of thresholds

title: Microbiome meta-analysis and cross-disease comparison enabled by the SIAMCAT machine learning toolbox
what_they_do: SIAMCAT toolbox; cross-study holdout; best practices for microbiome ML
how_we_differ: Tool supports external validation but offers no threshold transport

title: Performance of gut microbiome as an independent diagnostic tool for 20 diseases: cross-cohort validation of machine-learning classifiers
what_they_do: 330 cross-cohort validations across 20 diseases; external AUROC mean ~0.64
how_we_differ: AUROC only; we target operating-point drift

title: Best practices for developing microbiome-based disease diagnostic classifiers through machine learning
what_they_do: Systematic evaluation of normalisation, confounder adjustment, algorithms on external performance
how_we_differ: Generalisation via preprocessing; no deployment threshold method

title: Adjusting batch effects in microarray expression data using empirical Bayes methods
what_they_do: ComBat: empirical-Bayes location/scale batch adjustment of features
how_we_differ: ComBat applies location-scale correction to FEATURES and needs batch membership with both classes; we apply an affine shift to the classifier SCORE, fit by ML on unlabeled target scores with prevalence as free parameter

title: ComBat-seq: batch effect adjustment for RNA-seq count data
what_they_do: Negative-binomial ComBat for counts
how_we_differ: Feature-level; not threshold/score-level

title: Population structure discovery in meta-analyzed microbial communities and inflammatory bowel disease using MMUPHin
what_they_do: Microbiome-specific ComBat-like batch correction and meta-analysis
how_we_differ: Feature-level harmonisation requires pooling raw data; does not guarantee target specificity; we work on frozen classifier scores

title: Batch effects removal for microbiome data via conditional quantile regression
what_they_do: ConQuR: quantile-regression batch removal for microbiome counts
how_we_differ: Feature-level; needs reference batch and covariates

title: Correcting for batch effects in case-control microbiome studies
what_they_do: Percentile normalisation of features to within-study controls
how_we_differ: Uses LABELLED local controls as the reference (closest analogue of our few-control setting) but at feature level and needs many controls; we use n controls or none at score level

title: Managing batch effects in microbiome data
what_they_do: Review of batch effects/correction in microbiome
how_we_differ: Review; motivates problem

title: PLSDA-batch: a multivariate framework to correct for batch effects in microbiome data
what_they_do: Multivariate batch correction preserving treatment effect
how_we_differ: Feature-level

title: Benchmark of data processing methods and machine learning models for gut microbiome-based diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease
what_they_do: LODO benchmark of preprocessing and batch correction for IBD classifiers
how_we_differ: AUROC; no thresholds

title: Cross-cohort generalization limitations in gut microbiome-based Alzheimer's disease classifiers
what_they_do: LOCO transfer and batch adjustment in 16S AD classifiers
how_we_differ: AUROC transportability only

title: Instance-based transfer learning enables cross-cohort early detection of colorectal cancer
what_they_do: Instance-based transfer learning using target cohort samples to reduce cohort shift for CRC
how_we_differ: Retrains model using target data (labelled); we keep the model frozen and transport only the operating point, label-free or with few controls

title: Cross-cohort analysis identifies shared gut microbial signatures and validates microbial risk scores for colorectal cancer
what_they_do: Cross-cohort microbial risk scores for CRC
how_we_differ: Risk-score validation; no threshold transport

title: Gut microbiome-based machine learning model for early colorectal cancer and adenoma screening
what_they_do: RF CRC/adenoma model; external specificity 0.96 vs 0.97 internal for one task, 0.21 specificity for another
how_we_differ: Anecdotal evidence of threshold drift; no method; supports our motivation

title: Microbiota-assisted screening for colorectal neoplasia: advanced adenoma as the key translational endpoint - a narrative review
what_they_do: Narrative review; recommends prespecified thresholds and intercept-only recalibration under prevalence differences
how_we_differ: States the need; offers no method or evaluation; our work operationalises it

title: A universal oral microbiome-based signature for periodontitis
what_they_do: Cross-cohort oral microbiome classifier, multi-cohort validation
how_we_differ: AUROC-based generalisation

title: Two stable gut microbiome guilds predict liver tumor class and treatment responses
what_they_do: Guild-based cross-cohort classifiers
how_we_differ: No threshold transport

title: A decade-scale audit of microbiome AI-readiness
what_they_do: Audit of 2,896 human microbiome studies (2012-2025) for AI-ready metadata deposition; 85.5% of samples not reusable for cross-cohort AI
how_we_differ: Data-reuse audit, unrelated to thresholds; useful only to motivate scarcity of labelled local data

title: Discovery of robust and highly specific microbiome signatures of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
what_they_do: Cross-cohort NAFLD signatures with specificity emphasis
how_we_differ: Disease specificity, not site threshold

title: Effects of data transformation and model selection on feature importance in microbiome classification data
what_they_do: Benchmark of transformations/models
how_we_differ: Unrelated to thresholds

title: Statistical modeling of gut microbiota for personalized health status monitoring
what_they_do: Statistical modelling for health monitoring
how_we_differ: Monitoring not threshold transfer

title: Validation and updating of predictive logistic regression models: a study on sample size and shrinkage
what_they_do: Recalibration-in-the-large, logistic recalibration, revision; sample size
how_we_differ: Requires labelled local outcomes; we provide label-free and n-control variants targeted at a specificity constraint

title: Updating methods improved the performance of a clinical prediction model in new patients
what_they_do: Hierarchy of updating methods with local labelled data
how_we_differ: Labelled updating; ours targets operating point, label-free option

title: A calibration hierarchy for risk models was defined: from utopia to empirical data
what_they_do: Defines mean/weak/moderate/strong calibration
how_we_differ: Conceptual framing; we target specificity not calibration

title: Calibration: the Achilles heel of predictive analytics
what_they_do: Argues calibration and local updating essential
how_we_differ: Motivational

title: External validation of clinical prediction models using big datasets from e-health records or IPD meta-analysis: opportunities and challenges
what_they_do: Heterogeneity of performance across clusters; IPD-MA validation
how_we_differ: Shows between-site heterogeneity of calibration; we quantify specificity drift and fix it

title: A new framework to enhance the interpretation of external validation studies of clinical prediction models
what_they_do: Relatedness vs transportability framework
how_we_differ: Interpretation framework only

title: Variation of a test's sensitivity and specificity with disease prevalence
what_they_do: Empirical evidence that Se/Sp vary with prevalence/setting
how_we_differ: Motivational evidence; supports overdispersion finding

title: Decision curve analysis: a novel method for evaluating prediction models
what_they_do: Net-benefit evaluation at thresholds
how_we_differ: We report per-1000 harms; related evaluation philosophy

title: Unsupervised detection and correction of model calibration shift at test-time
what_they_do: Label-free correction of calibration shift of sepsis model at a new hospital using cohort-level features to hit a target PPV
how_we_differ: Closest clinical label-free recalibration; uses feature/cohort meta-regression across many hospitals, not a score mixture; targets PPV; not microbiome. Must cite and compare conceptually

title: Safe and reliable transport of prediction models to new healthcare settings without the need to collect new labeled data
what_they_do: Weighted conformal prediction with density ratios on unlabeled target data to flag unreliable predictions
how_we_differ: Reliability flags under covariate shift; not threshold/specificity control; needs feature density ratios

title: Against reflexive recalibration: towards a causal framework for addressing miscalibration
what_they_do: Argues recalibration choice should depend on shift mechanism (label vs covariate shift)
how_we_differ: Conceptual; supports explicit shift model (our a,b + prevalence decomposition)

title: Adjusting the outputs of a classifier to new a priori probabilities: a simple procedure
what_they_do: EM estimation of new class priors from unlabeled data; posterior adjustment
how_we_differ: Assumes pure label shift (p(x|y) fixed); our model adds an affine score shift (a,b) so class-conditionals can move; Saerens is our baseline

title: Detecting and correcting for label shift with black box predictors (BBSE)
what_they_do: Confusion-matrix moment estimator of target priors
how_we_differ: Label shift only; no threshold re-targeting under score shift

title: Regularized learning for domain adaptation under label shifts (RLLS)
what_they_do: Regularised importance weight estimation for label shift
how_we_differ: Same assumption gap as BBSE

title: Maximum likelihood with bias-corrected calibration is hard-to-beat at label shift adaptation
what_they_do: MLLS with calibration; EM prior estimation
how_we_differ: Our method is an MLLS extension with an affine conditional-shift nuisance; must show where pure MLLS fails (score shift)

title: A unified view of label shift estimation
what_they_do: Unifies BBSE and MLLS; error analysis
how_we_differ: Theory for label shift only

title: Domain adaptation with conditional distribution matching and generalized label shift
what_they_do: Generalised label shift: p(z|y) invariant in a representation
how_we_differ: GLS requires learned invariant representation; we allow parametric affine shift of the score

title: Domain adaptation under target and conditional shift
what_they_do: Joint target (prior) shift + location-scale conditional shift (LS-TarS/GeTarS) estimated from unlabeled target data via kernel mean matching
how_we_differ: CONCEPTUALLY CLOSEST: location-scale conditional shift + prior shift. Differences: applied to features with kernel matching, goal is classifier accuracy; ours is 1-D score, parametric ML, explicit specificity target, per-site evaluation, microbiome. Must cite prominently

title: Domain-shift adaptation via linear transformations
what_they_do: Affine transformation of features between domains; notes unidentifiability unsupervised
how_we_differ: Feature-level, equal priors assumed; we jointly fit prior and affine score shift; identifiability via transported class shapes

title: Quantifying counts and costs via classification
what_they_do: Quantification (prevalence estimation) incl. threshold-based adjusted count methods
how_we_differ: Quantification only; our goal is threshold not prevalence

title: A review on quantification learning
what_they_do: Review of quantification methods incl. mixture-model approaches (HDy etc.)
how_we_differ: Mixture-model quantifiers (e.g. HDy) fit class-conditional score distributions to target scores under label shift; ours adds score location-scale shift and uses estimate to set threshold

title: Leveraging unlabeled data to predict out-of-distribution performance (ATC)
what_they_do: Average thresholded confidence: label-free accuracy estimate via a confidence threshold
how_we_differ: Estimates accuracy, not specificity at a fixed rule; multiclass vision

title: Predicting with confidence on unseen distributions (DoC)
what_they_do: Difference of confidences to predict accuracy drop
how_we_differ: Accuracy estimation only

title: Confidence-based performance estimation (CBPE) documentation
what_they_do: Label-free confusion-matrix estimation from calibrated probabilities (assumes no concept shift)
how_we_differ: Estimates realised Sp/FPR assuming calibration holds; does not adapt threshold; breaks under score shift

title: Label-free estimation of clinically relevant performance metrics under distribution shifts
what_they_do: Generalises ATC/CBPE to full confusion matrix for chest X-ray; shows failure under some shifts
how_we_differ: Estimates metrics, does not re-set threshold; imaging

title: Deployment of image analysis algorithms under prevalence shifts
what_they_do: Estimate deployment prevalence label-free and re-adjust calibration and decision threshold
how_we_differ: Same workflow idea (estimate prevalence -> adjust threshold) but pure prevalence shift (no score shift), threshold re-optimised for cost not specificity guarantee, imaging

title: Navigating prevalence shifts in image analysis algorithm deployment
what_they_do: 30 tasks; shows prevalence shift harms calibration, threshold and assessment; prevalence-aware workflow
how_we_differ: As above; our key extra is site-specific score shift (realised specificity of controls changes even without prevalence change)

title: Test-time adaptation with calibration of medical image classification nets for label distribution shift
what_they_do: Test-time adaptation to unknown label distribution in medical imaging
how_we_differ: Multiclass accuracy; no operating point

title: Doubly flexible estimation under label shift
what_they_do: Semiparametric efficient estimation under label shift
how_we_differ: Theory, label shift only

title: A generalized Neyman-Pearson criterion for optimal domain adaptation
what_they_do: NP-type criterion for domain adaptation without target labels
how_we_differ: Theoretical; different shift model

title: When normality shifts: multi-level WavLM modeling for open-world audio deepfake detection
what_they_do: Tests unlabeled quantile recalibration of a detector threshold to recover target FPR when positives rare
how_we_differ: Same 'local quantile of unlabeled pool' baseline in another domain; supports that quantile works at low prevalence, fails otherwise; no mixture model

title: Online shift detection and conformal adaptation for deployed safety classifiers
what_they_do: KS drift alarm + conformal threshold adjustment via density ratios, no new labels
how_we_differ: Text classifiers; density-ratio weighting; we use parametric score-shift

title: Neyman-Pearson classification algorithms and NP receiver operating characteristics
what_they_do: NP umbrella algorithm: order-statistic threshold on held-out class-0 scores guaranteeing type-I error with high probability
how_we_differ: Our few-control conformal baseline is exactly this applied to n local controls; novelty is in comparing with label-free and in sample-size requirements (n>=~45 for 90% spec at 95% conf)

title: Conformal prediction under covariate shift
what_they_do: Weighted conformal with likelihood ratios
how_we_differ: Covariate shift; needs density ratios; we model score shift

title: Distribution-free uncertainty quantification for classification under label shift
what_they_do: Conformal/calibration under label shift with estimated weights
how_we_differ: Label shift only; class-conditional coverage

title: A gentle introduction to conformal prediction and distribution-free uncertainty quantification
what_they_do: Review incl. conformal risk control
how_we_differ: Background

title: Testing for outliers with conformal p-values
what_they_do: Conformal p-values with FDR/FPR guarantees from reference inliers
how_we_differ: Theory for calibration-set based thresholds; supports the n-control conformal baseline

title: Neyman-Pearson classification under both null and alternative distributions shift
what_they_do: Transfer NP classification with LABELLED target samples from both classes; adaptive to source informativeness
how_we_differ: Needs labelled target data; no parametric score shift

title: Shift-adjusted Neyman-Pearson classifiers via single index modeling (SACSIM)
what_they_do: Adapts NP decision rule to target population using a small UNLABELED target sample + minimal auxiliary info (e.g. prevalence), semiparametric single-index model; cancer detection example
how_we_differ: CLOSEST statistical prior art for label-free NP threshold transfer. Differences: covariate-shift/density-ratio on features with single-index model and auxiliary info; ours: no features needed at target beyond frozen score, affine score shift + prevalence estimated jointly, microbiome multi-site benchmark. Must cite and position against

title: Fecal immunochemical test positivity thresholds: an international survey of population-based screening programs
what_they_do: FIT thresholds range 8.5-120 ug/g across 38 programmes; 9 sites had to change initial threshold
how_we_differ: Motivation: thresholds are site-specific in real screening; no method

title: Effect of sex, age, and positivity threshold on fecal immunochemical test accuracy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
what_they_do: Meta-analysis of FIT sensitivity/specificity vs threshold
how_we_differ: Motivation; per-1000 harm framing

title: Is it appropriate to use fixed assay cut-offs for estimating seroprevalence?
what_they_do: Mixture models vs fixed cut-offs for serology without gold standard
how_we_differ: Two-component mixture on unlabeled assay values; no source transport of class shapes or affine shift; prevalence focus

title: Estimating the cumulative incidence of SARS-CoV-2 with imperfect serological tests: exploiting cutoff-free approaches
what_they_do: Mixture models (with control distributions) outperform cut-off methods for prevalence
how_we_differ: Uses reference distributions from controls/cases (transported shapes) - similar machinery; target is prevalence not operating point; serology

title: Bayesian binary mixture models as a flexible alternative to cut-off analysis of ELISA results, a case study of Seoul orthohantavirus
what_they_do: Bayesian two-component mixture to classify ELISA values without cut-off
how_we_differ: Unsupervised mixture on raw assay; ours transports class shapes from a labelled source and models site shift

title: No need for a gold-standard test: on the mining of diagnostic test performance indices merely based on the distribution of the test value
what_they_do: Fit two latent subpopulations to test-value distribution to get Se/Sp without gold standard
how_we_differ: Mixture-based Se/Sp estimation; no source knowledge, no threshold transfer

title: Receiver operator characteristic (ROC) analysis without truth
what_they_do: Estimates ROC from unlabeled ratings via latent binormal mixture
how_we_differ: Classic latent-class ROC; we add source-anchored shapes and affine site shift for operating-point transfer

title: Indirect methods for reference interval determination - review and recommendations
what_they_do: Indirect estimation of the healthy distribution from mixed routine lab data (mixture/truncation)
how_we_differ: Analogous label-free estimation of 'control' distribution from unlabeled pool; univariate analytes, no classifier

title: RefineR: a novel algorithm for reference interval estimation from real-world data
what_they_do: Inverse modelling of non-pathological distribution in mixed data
how_we_differ: Same as above; we additionally exploit source class shapes
